anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used to format this dataset; it does not describe the IACKD dataset itself.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-format specification extension used to organize this dataset, not a paper describing the IACKD intention-action conflict dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG data were recorded and converted to BIDS format using MNE and mne-bids, with task stimuli presented via PsychoPy (version 2023.2). Data processing was conducted in Python 3.10.

citation_details.title: Intention-Action Conflict EEG-Hand Kinematics Dataset for Unimanual Control under Congruent and Incongruent Conditions
citation_details.author: Mengpu Cai, Rongrong Fu, Yaodong Wang, Bin Lu, Saiwei Guo, Fangyao Xu
citation_details.abstract: The Intention-Action Conflict EEG-Hand Kinematics Dataset (IACKD) is a joint resource for studying congruent and incongruent intention-action conditions during unimanual control. It comprises 7,040 trials from 15 participants. Each trial includes a 1-s pre-movement period and a movement-execution period. A target frame and a controllable ball define the task; ball color cues congruency (red = same direction; yellow = opposite). EEG was recorded with a 32-channel Compumedics Neuroscan system at 1024 Hz, and 3-D hand trajectories were captured with Leap Motion at 170 Hz. Streams are time-aligned, and complete preprocessing and alignment scripts are provided. Technical validation includes readiness potentials at C3/C4/Cz, μ/β-band ERD/ERS with post-movement β rebound, sub-30-ms cross-modal residuals on >99.375% of trials, and expected completion-time differences between congruent and incongruent conditions. IACKD is intended for reuse in intention decoding, continuous trajectory decoding, and evaluation of decoder robustness under conflict or perturbed feedback.

citation_details.title: Dataset for Multiple Basketball Motor Observation and Motor Imagery Based on Functional Connectivity Analysis
citation_details.author: Jiaqi Wang, Ming Tang, Lingrong Jia, Jinxiang Zhang, Cheng Cheng, Jiahui Han
citation_details.abstract: This study presents an electroencephalography (EEG) dataset collected during motor imagery (MI) and motor observation (MO) of basketball-specific actions, designed to support functional connectivity research and facilitate brain-computer interface (BCI) development. Thirty-five healthy right-handed participants completed three experimental protocols: single-hand dribbling, bilateral ball tapping (throwing the ball from one hand to the other), and two-person passing. The three protocols included different types of MI and MO tasks, yielding 1,560 trials per participant with a total recording duration of approximately 70 min. The dataset provides raw recordings, preprocessed data, and functional connectivity matrices based on phase-locking values (PLV) across multiple frequency bands and time windows. Additional metadata included demographic information and scores from the KVIQ-20, which assesses motor-imagery ability. This dataset enables investigations into the neural mechanisms underlying MI and MO in ecologically valid sports contexts and the evaluation of functional connectivity metrics and may even offer opportunities for the development of functional connectivity-based MI-BCI applications.
